title: How to use Keynote for students on Mac: a guide for version 15.4
metaTitle: Keynote for students on Mac: tips and tricks for better presentations
description: Master Keynote for students on Mac with our guide. Learn essential shortcuts, design tips, and how to use Lazur to speed up your presentation workflow.
intro: Keynote for students on Mac is a powerful, free tool for creating professional presentations. It is built into every Mac and gives you over 40 themes to start your work.
tldr: Keynote is free and pre-installed on your Mac.
Use keyboard shortcuts to save time on common tasks.
Master the master slide to keep your design consistent.
Lazur helps you find tools and dictate notes while you work.

blocks.text: Getting started with Keynote for students on Mac

Keynote 15.4 is the latest version for macOS 26. It is a standalone app you download from the Mac App Store. You do not need the old iWork suite anymore. Open it and select a template from the theme chooser. If you want to change your layout, right-click the toolbar and select Customize Toolbar to add your most used items.

items: Option + Command + P: Start your slideshow.
Shift + Command + ?: Open the Keynote User Guide.
B: Pause the show with a black screen.
W: Pause the show with a white screen.

blocks.text: You can also create your own shortcuts. Go to System Settings > Keyboard > Shortcuts > App Shortcuts. Click the plus button to add a command for Keynote. Remember that you cannot override system-level shortcuts.
Speed up your workflow with Lazur

Lazur lives in the notch of your Mac. Hold Option + Command to ask it where a button is. It draws a circle around the tool so you do not have to hunt for it. If you need to write presenter notes, hold the fn key to dictate your thoughts. Lazur types them out at your cursor.

Consistency is key. Use the master slide to set your fonts and colors for the whole deck. This saves you from editing every slide individually. If you are collaborating, use the share button to work on the file with others. Check your layout often to make sure images and text are aligned.

Sometimes files will not open. Check if the file is in iCloud or on your local drive. If it still fails, restart your Mac in Safe Mode to rule out background app conflicts. If you are struggling with advanced features like Magic Move, look for the animation tab in the right sidebar. You can set the transition type there.

Keynote allows you to add videos and tables easily. You can mask images to fit them into specific shapes. If you need to present on a second display, go to Play > Play Slideshow on Second Display. Make sure your cables are secure before you start.

When you are done, you can export your file to different formats. Go to File > Export To. You can choose PDF, PowerPoint, or even a movie file. This is helpful if you need to share your work with a professor who uses Windows or a different app.

faq.question: Is Keynote free for students?
faq.answer: Yes, Keynote is free and available on the Mac App Store for all Mac users.

faq.question: Does Keynote work on Windows?
faq.answer: Keynote is for macOS, but you can export your presentations as PowerPoint files to share with Windows users.

faq.question: Can Lazur help me with my presentation?
faq.answer: Lazur can help you find tools in the menu, dictate text, and explain how to use specific features like animations or transitions.
